candidates.claim: Share FlashMLA decode plans across compatible KV-cache groups within one metadata-building pass, conditional on the pinned H200 runner still creating duplicate plans. The supplied patch implements per-pass holder sharing; the author reports fewer planner launches on H20 TP8, using synthetic acceptance for serving measurements. That establishes an implementation mechanism, not an H200 benefit. Unlike small-head kernels, this change does not require TP4 or TP8 and can plausibly apply to TP1. Its value depends on exposed redundant planner work under real DSpark rejection. Reuse must preserve equal live lengths, masks and replay state, rather than merely matching tensor shapes. First inspect baseline membership and builder dispatch; then compare unchanged execution with sharing alone, preserving all serving settings and measuring primary-workload latency and throughput.

candidates.claim: Test direct paged candidate-only indexer scoring as a conditional replacement for dense scoring followed by masking in consumer layers. The supplied #62463 patch describes reading candidate K in place and retaining device-resident live lengths; #62000 instead gathers K before scoring. These are competing implementations of the same work-elimination mechanism, not cumulative optimizations. H20 evidence is conflicting: gathering regressed at one request, while direct scoring's lower ITL came from tiny samples and did not consistently improve throughput. The transfer hypothesis is that avoiding both discarded scoring and intermediate K copies helps eligible H200 long-context decode. First establish actual indexer shapes, cache format and baseline dispatch. Keep dense scoring as the short-context comparator and default; require native 8K/1K evidence before claiming a useful change to this deployment.

candidates.claim: Port or activate DeepSelect for eligible FP32 indexer top-k calls on SM90, only after checking the installed selector and extension build. The supplied vLLM patch adds a Hopper availability path and explicit dtype, width, k and alignment checks. Its value would come from faster selection over unchanged logits, independently of attention-head padding or candidate scoring. However, the DeepSelect library's headline H20 results concern small-batch BF16 inputs, while this integration requires FP32; a commenter also reports a competing radix advantage at k=2048. Therefore, compare against the fastest eligible existing vLLM backend chosen on calibration workloads, not merely torch.topk. Preserve existing fallbacks and isolate this selector change initially with dense scoring. Any later compact-logit combination needs separate confirmation because the remaining selection workload is different.
